promptHead: Athlete goal: 5K (Corrowmore Harvest 5K) on Sun Nov 15 2026, 8 weeks out, target run the whole way.

new.headline: Three easy runs keep building endurance while staying safe after illness.

flags.title: Volume
flags.detail: keep total weekly mileage moderate and increase only by a few percent.

flags.title: Symptoms
flags.detail: monitor cough, fever or fatigue; if any worsen, take an extra rest day.

flags.title: Heart rate
flags.detail: stay in easy zone 1‑2 throughout the week.

flags.title: Cadence
flags.detail: finish the Wednesday run with 4 strides to build turnover.

answers.question: Can I do all three runs next week and add the two I missed?
answers.answer: Yes, you can run the three scheduled sessions next week. Adding the two missed runs might overload you, especially after a recent illness, so keep to the scheduled days and consider a light walk if you feel up to it.

new.analysis: The athlete missed Wednesday and Saturday from the prior week, dropping from three planned runs to two completed. They reported lingering cough and fever from a recent illness, but no pain or new symptoms. In a build phase with a new runner, we keep volume modest and stay in easy zones. Three easy runs are the core of the week – Mon, Wed, Sat – with the rest days providing recovery. The question was whether to add the missed runs back; adding two extra sessions would exceed the build volume and could raise fatigue. Instead, doing the scheduled runs and optionally a short walk will help catch up without overloading. Heart rate should stay in zone 1‑2; short strides on the Wednesday run improve turnover. The plan includes a slightly longer Saturday run to increase endurance while keeping effort easy. We add a safety callout for the lingering cough: if it worsens or new symptoms appear, seek a professional.

days.notes: keep pace under 6 min/km, flat route. Builds aerobic base.
